In its weekly measles update, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said there are now 1,514 confirmed measles cases in the United States reported this year, with 23 new cases reported in the past week. Eighty-six percent of the cases have been part of 40 outbreaks reported to the CDC. Of note, 92% of case-patients are unvaccinated or have unknown vaccination status, 4% have only one measles, mumps, and rubella dose, and 4% were fully vaccinated. Georgia's health department reported three more measles infections with links to its most recent case; two patients were unvaccinated and one had an unknown vaccination status. This is an official CDC health advisory. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is issuing this Health Alert Network (HAN) Health Advisory to notify clinicians, public health officials, and potential travelers about a measles outbreak in Texas and New Mexico and offer guidance for prevention and monitoring. As of March 7, 2025, Texas and New Mexico have reported 208 confirmed cases associated with this outbreak (198 in Texas and 10 in New Mexico). top_result_summaries.title: Measles Update — United States, January 1–April 17, 2025 | MMWR
top_result_summaries.snippet: Although measles was declared eliminated in the United States in 2000, large outbreaks with 50 or more cases have become more frequent, especially in close-knit communities with low vaccination coverage. During January 1–April 17, 2025, a total of 800 measles cases were reported in the United States, the second highest annual case count in 25 years; 82% were associated with an ongoing outbreak in close-knit communities with low vaccination coverage in New Mexico, Oklahoma, and Texas. As of April 17, a total of 800 cases have been reported in the United States in 2025; 654 (82%) cases in New Mexico, Oklahoma, and Texas have been associated with the ongoing outbreak. Overall, 771 (96%) patients have been unvaccinated or had unknown vaccination status (77% were unvaccinated, and 14% had unknown vaccination status when excluding 590 cases reported by Texas, which requires explicit consent by law [i.e., opt-in] to enroll in the Texas Immunization Registry), 85 (11%) patients have been hospitalized, and three patients have died.

Although measles was declared eliminated in the United States in 2000, measles cases and outbreaks continue to occur in the United States due to unvaccinated international travelers. top_result_summaries.title: 2025 Southwest United States measles outbreak - Wikipedia
top_result_summaries.snippet: # 2025 Southwest United States measles outbreak. | 2025–26 United States measles outbreak | |. | Location | United States (Texas, New Mexico, Oklahoma, Kansas), Mexico (Chihuahua "Chihuahua (state)")) |. In January 2025, cases of measles began to appear in Texas and neighboring states in the United States. The outbreak became one of the largest in the country since 2000, when the United States declared the disease eliminated in the country. In March, cases linked to the outbreak were announced in Oklahoma, the Mexican state of Chihuahua "Chihuahua (state)"), and Kansas. Cases were concentrated in the Texas Mennonite community, and officials believed the disease was first imported from an outbreak in a Mennonite community in Ontario, Canada. More than 99 individuals were hospitalized, and three died: two children in Lubbock (a six-year-old and an eight-year-old) and an adult in Lea County, New Mexico. The Texas outbreak involved the measles genotype D8, and was linked to cases in New Mexico, Kansas, Oklahoma, and Chihuahua, Mexico "Chihuahua (state)").

decision.decision_reason: Iteration 1 produced strong national-level coverage (CDC HAN advisory, MMWR update, CDC surveillance page, CIDRAP weekly updates, JHU tracker, Wikipedia outbreak article, MSK library guide with county-level detail) and confirmed the primary outbreak locus (Texas/New Mexico/Oklahoma/Kansas Mennonite community). However, several target fields remain underserved by the current candidate set: (1) subnational_location and locality granularity for states beyond Texas — Oklahoma, New Mexico, Kansas, and other states with smaller clusters are represented only in passing; (2) state-level official press releases for Oklahoma (OSDH), New Mexico (NMDOH), and Kansas (KDHE) that would carry authoritative confirmed case counts and dates for those jurisdictions; (3) the Texas DSHS appeared only once and its snippet did not carry Q1 2025 case-count tables; (4) PAHO and WHO appeared (2 results each) but their snippets did not confirm Q1-specific case totals for the US; (5) hospitalization data at the subnational level is absent beyond the MMWR aggregate (85 hospitalized through April 17); (6) the deaths field (3 deaths: 2 children in Lubbock, 1 adult in Lea County, NM) needs corroboration from state-level official sources. A second iteration targeting these specific gaps — state health department pages for TX/NM/OK/KS, PAHO Q1 situation report, and MMWR/CDC early-2025 weekly reports — will materially improve subnational_location, locality, date_reported, deaths, and hospitalizations field coverage within the Q1 2025 window. Budget allows one more iteration (max 4 queries).
decision.coverage_assessment: National-level case counts and the dominant Southwest outbreak are well-covered. CDC HAN advisory (March 7, 2025: 208 confirmed in TX+NM), MMWR (800 cases through April 17, 85 hospitalized, 3 deaths), and CIDRAP weekly updates provide strong national anchors. Subnational coverage is partial: Texas DSHS appeared once without a detailed snippet; Oklahoma, New Mexico, and Kansas state-level official pages are absent from the candidate set. The MSK library guide provides useful county-level detail (Harris/Houston, Gaines/Lubbock, Rockwall, Travis in TX; Howard County MD; Oklahoma March 11 link) but is a secondary aggregator, not a primary state agency source. Deaths (3) and hospitalizations (85+) are confirmed at national level but not corroborated by state-level official sources for the Q1 window specifically.
decision.source_diversity_assessment: Good diversity across source types: CDC official (5 results), CIDRAP (3), JHU IVAC tracker (3), Wikipedia (2), MSK library guide (2), AAP (2), PAHO (2), WHO (2), Texas DSHS (1), SC DPH (1), news outlets (abc7, forbes, contagionlive, reliefweb). Missing: Oklahoma OSDH, New Mexico DOH, Kansas KDHE, and New Mexico Lea County-specific official pages. PAHO/WHO snippets did not surface Q1-specific US situation reports. ProMED and HealthMap (structured databases) are absent but lower priority given strong official coverage.
decision.trustworthiness_assessment: High-trust sources dominate: CDC.gov (5 results including HAN advisory and MMWR), CIDRAP (peer-reviewed public health news citing CDC), JHU IVAC (academic tracker citing official sources). Wikipedia is useful for narrative context but not for numeric field extraction. MSK library guide is a secondary aggregator — useful for locality detail but must be traced to primary sources. AAP Red Book snippet references 2026 data and is out of scope for Q1 2025. YouTube result is not extractable. No low-credibility or fringe sources detected.
decision.disease_location_time_fit_assessment: Disease fit: Excellent — all accepted results are measles-specific. Location fit: Good nationally; partial subnationally (TX dominant, NM/OK/KS underrepresented in official sources). Time fit: Partial — MMWR covers Jan 1–Apr 17 (extends beyond Q1 but includes Q1 data); CDC HAN advisory is dated March 7, 2025 (within Q1); CIDRAP result references 1,514 cases (a later cumulative figure beyond Q1). Need to surface sources specifically reporting Q1 2025 (Jan–Mar) case counts and dates, particularly early outbreak reports from January–February 2025 for Texas and the initial Oklahoma/NM case announcements.
decision.corroboration_potential_assessment: The 3 deaths (2 Lubbock children, 1 Lea County NM adult) appear in Wikipedia and MMWR snippets but need corroboration from Texas DSHS and New Mexico DOH official pages. The 85 hospitalization figure from MMWR needs state-level corroboration. The March 7 CDC HAN figure of 208 confirmed (198 TX, 10 NM) is a strong anchor for Q1 but needs Texas DSHS and NMDOH press releases to confirm at the state level. Oklahoma's March 11 link to West Texas outbreak (2 cases per MSK guide) needs OSDH corroboration.

top_result_summaries.title: Measles Outbreak in a Child Care Facility — Lubbock, Texas, March–April 2025  | MMWR
top_result_summaries.snippet: During March–April 2025, eight confirmed measles cases linked to a child care facility were reported in Lubbock, Texas. On March 21, 2025, Lubbock Public Health (LPH) in Texas received a report of a child care attendee aged 3 years, with fever, rash, cough, coryza, conjunctivitis, otitis media, and diarrhea who received a positive test result for measles by real-time reverse transcription–polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). Six additional children who attended the same child care facility and the grandfather of one of the children were confirmed by RT-PCR testing to have measles. On March 21, 2025, Lubbock Public Health (LPH) in Texas was notified of a suspected measles case in a child aged 3 years (index patient, patient A) who had fever, rash, cough, coryza, conjunctivitis, otitis media, and diarrhea. During March 25–29, LPH was notified of two additional suspected measles cases (patients B and C); both cases occurred in children who attended the same child care facility as the index patient, including a child in the same classroom as the index patient (patient B) and a sibling of the index patient (patient C) who was exposed at home (Table).

top_result_summaries.title: 2025 Southwest United States measles outbreak - Wikipedia
top_result_summaries.snippet: # 2025 Southwest United States measles outbreak. | 2025–26 United States measles outbreak | |. | Location | United States (Texas, New Mexico, Oklahoma, Kansas), Mexico (Chihuahua "Chihuahua (state)")) |. In January 2025, cases of measles began to appear in Texas and neighboring states in the United States. The outbreak became one of the largest in the country since 2000, when the United States declared the disease eliminated in the country. In March, cases linked to the outbreak were announced in Oklahoma, the Mexican state of Chihuahua "Chihuahua (state)"), and Kansas. Cases were concentrated in the Texas Mennonite community, and officials believed the disease was first imported from an outbreak in a Mennonite community in Ontario, Canada. More than 99 individuals were hospitalized, and three died: two children in Lubbock (a six-year-old and an eight-year-old) and an adult in Lea County, New Mexico. The Texas outbreak involved the measles genotype D8, and was linked to cases in New Mexico, Kansas, Oklahoma, and Chihuahua, Mexico "Chihuahua (state)").

A day care facility in a Texas county that's part of the measles outbreak has multiple cases, including children too young to be fully vaccinated, public health officials say. West Texas is in the middle of a still-growing measles outbreak with 505 cases reported on Tuesday. As of Friday, there were seven cases at a day care where one young child who was infectious gave it to two other children before it spread to other classrooms, Lubbock Public Health director Katherine Wells said. decision.coverage_assessment:

• disease: Confirmed — Measles, across all accepted sources.
• country: United States — confirmed across all sources.
• subnational_location: Texas (primary), New Mexico (Lea County death confirmed via ArcGIS snippet and nmhealth.org), Oklahoma (OSDH March 11 link via MSK library guide), Kansas (coronavirus.kdheks.gov appeared in iteration 2 domain counts). Maryland (Howard County) also surfaced.
• locality: Gaines County TX, Lubbock TX, West Texas (Mennonite community), Lea County NM, Harris/Houston TX, Rockwall TX, Travis TX, Howard County MD — all identified from snippets.
• date_reported: Multiple Q1 2025 dates captured: January 2025 onset (Wikipedia, MSK guide), February 26 (first TX death — DSHS news release referenced in DSHS snippet, YouTube KSAT12 video, abc7ny.com), March 4 (Lubbock Online — 159 TX cases), March 6 (NM Lea County death — ArcGIS snippet), March 7 (CDC HAN advisory — 208 TX+NM cases), March 21 (Lubbock child care facility index case — MMWR mm7521a1).
• cases_confirmed: 124 (as of ~Feb 26, DSHS via abc7ny), 159 TX / Gaines County >100 (March 4, Lubbock Online), 208 TX+NM (March 7, CDC HAN), 800 total Jan 1–Apr 17 (MMWR mm7414a1 — partially outside Q1 window but Q1 sub-period data extractable), 505 TX (PBS — post-Q1), 750 TX final (Texas Tribune — post-Q1, useful for context only).
• deaths: 3 total confirmed — 2 children in Lubbock (first death Feb 26 per DSHS/abc7ny/YouTube; second death April 6 per DSHS snippet — outside Q1 window), 1 adult in Lea County NM (March 6 per ArcGIS snippet).
